title: Region preference opt-in experiment notes
content:
Purpose

This doc captures the rationale, hypothesis, and runbook for a small-scale experiment that surfaces a customer-level region preference (opt-in) flow during Private onboarding. The goal is to measure whether offering a clear, low-friction way for customers to express a region preference reduces support friction and improves compliance telemetry (fewer pinning exceptions) without materially increasing provisioning complexity or SLA violations.

Background and why this is different

We have a set of mature internal playbooks that cover strict region pin enforcement, operator runbooks for eviction, and regional fallback policies. Those are primarily engineering-facing and assume a backend-first, queued exception flow. This experiment flips the UX: we test an explicit customer-centered moment during sign-up/onboarding where customers can state a soft region preference (not a hard legal pin) that is then used by our routing heuristics and onboarding validation to reduce manual exception handling. It is intended to be non-binding, documented in the customer's agreement, and reversible.

Hypothesis

1) Exposing a simple region preference opt-in reduces the number of handshake exceptions we need to escalate to SRE/Legal by ~30% for pilot customers.
2) Customers who opt-in will have fewer region-mismatch support tickets and higher onboarding NPS.
3) There will be negligible impact to average request latency and resource utilization if we treat this as a soft-preference policy (best-effort affinity) rather than strict pinning.

Success metrics (primary and guardrails)

Primary metrics (measured per-customer and aggregated):
- Opt-in rate among pilot cohort (target 40–60%).
- Reduction in manual pinning exceptions opened in JIRA for pilot customers vs control (target -30%).
- Time-to-first-successful-region-anchored-deployment (median) for opt-in vs control (target no worse than baseline +10%).

Guardrail metrics (stop the experiment if thresholds breached):
- Increase in P99 latency for pilot customers > 15% vs baseline.
- Any increase in SLA violations (availability or error budget burn) attributable to the opt-in routing changes.
- >5% of opt-in customers later request full legal pinning within 7 days (indicates confusion/poor UX).

Experiment design and rollout plan

Cohort selection:
- 25 pilot customers from existing Private onboarding queue (mix of SMB and mid-market), selected by Solutions Eng.
- 25 matched control customers that receive the existing onboarding flow (no explicit preference surfaced).

Visibility & consent:
- During onboarding form, present an optional "Region preference" dropdown (data residency guidance + short hover text).
- Checkbox: "I understand this preference is a best-effort affinity and not a legal pin."
- Record preference in tenant metadata and in the onboarding acceptance email. Preference can be changed from the Console under Account > Region settings.

Routing behavior (implementation-level notes):
- Preference is implemented as a soft affinity tag used by Smart Router: route attempts will prefer matching pools when capacity is available.
- If matching capacity unavailable, fallback proceeds to nearest region per normal policy (no forced fail).
- Telemetry emitted: tenant.region.preference_set, tenant.region.preference_changed, route.attempt.preference_match, route.attempt.preference_miss.

Operator & SRE considerations:
- Operators can query tenants with preferences via admin CLI (cmd: admin-tenant-list --pref-region).
- Add an alert for unexpected preference-change spike (>10% of pilot tenants/day) to detect UX bugs or automated scripts.
- SRE playbook for a pilot tenant escalation remains: default to existing support-level runbook; only escalate to Legal if tenant requests a hard pin.

Customer communication templates (short forms used in experiment)

In-flow microcopy (onboarding form):
- Title: "Region preference (optional)"
- Helper: "Choose where you prefer your inference workload to run. This helps us route you to nearby capacity—it's not a legal guarantee. You can change this later in Account settings."

Email snippet (after onboarding completion):
- Subject: "Thanks — your region preference is recorded"
- Body: "We registered your preference to run workloads in {region}. This is a best-effort setting. If you need a legal residency guarantee, reach out to solutions@redwood-inference.com to start a pinning review."

Console copy (Account > Region settings):
- Heading: "Region preference"
- Subtext: "Set or change a best-effort routing preference. To request legally binding residency, open a support case."

Experiment instrumentation & telemetry plan

Events to collect (minimum):
- tenant.preference_set, tenant.preference_removed, tenant.preference_updated
- route.decision.reason (preference_match | capacity_miss | fallback_other)
- onboarding.support_ticket_created (tag to correlate with pilot cohort)

Dashboards & reports:
- Daily cohort dashboard showing opt-in %, preference distribution by region, preference match rate, support tickets per tenant, and onboarding NPS.
- Weekly summary for PM/PMM/SE: notable exceptions and open items.

QA & test matrix

- Unit tests for preference metadata read/write on tenant record.
- Integration test: simulate full request flow with pref region up and down; assert that preference_match event is produced when capacity present and fallback when not.
- E2E: onboarding form shows opt-in; acceptance email contains recorded preference.

Legal / Compliance notes (must include Legal before rolling out)

- The wording must clearly differentiate soft preference vs legal pin. Legal to approve the onboarding microcopy and the email snippet. Proposed language is intentionally conservative.
- Ensure telemetry and logs avoid leakage of customer PII—preference recording is a tenant-level attribute and should not contain user-provided free text.

Rollout checklist (pre-traffic)

- [ ] Legal copy approval obtained (owner: Priya Nair)
- [ ] SEs briefed and pilot customers selected (owner: Diego Ramirez)
- [ ] Router change merged behind feature flag (feature: tenant-pref-routing)
- [ ] Telemetry events instrumented and dashboards created (owner: Observability eng)
- [ ] Support & SRE notified and playbook updated (owners: SRE leads)

Rollback criteria and actions

Immediate rollback if any of the guardrails trigger. Rollback steps:
1) Flip feature flag tenant-pref-routing off (automated).
2) Notify pilot customers and internal stakeholders with current findings.
3) Revert any migrations that added preference fields to the tenant record if data integrity issues observed.

Open questions / decisions needed

- Should preferences be constrained to a fixed list (us-east1, europe-west1, apac-southeast1) or allow region groups (EU, NA, APAC)? Recommendation: fixed list to simplify routing and telemetry.
- What is the minimum guarantee we should state on the Console for opt-in customers? Proposed: "best-effort affinity; not a legal guarantee." Legal to finalize.
- Do we expose preference via public API? For pilot, keep internal-only (Console + admin API) to avoid accidental automation.

Next steps (short horizon)

- This week: Legal review + copy edits (Priya), pick pilot customers (Diego), create dashboards (Observability).
- Next two weeks: Deploy feature-flagged router logic to staging, run synthetic tests for capacity churn cases.
- After 3 weeks: Start pilot cohort onboarding and collect first-week telemetry, review metrics at 2-week cadence, iterate.

Notes to reviewers

- This is intentionally narrow — it's not a replacement for full pinning. The aim is to see whether a lightweight decluttering of the operator queue can be achieved by surfacing preference choices to customers earlier. Please focus reviews on: risk to SLA, clarity of customer-facing copy, and telemetry coverage.

Appendix: short sample support reply to common question

Q: "I selected EU preference but my jobs ran in us-east1 — why?"
A: "Preference is best-effort. If we cannot guarantee EU capacity at runtime, traffic may be routed to the nearest available region. If you need a legally binding residency guarantee, we can open a pinning request and discuss contract/SLA implications."
